description: UNRWA states Palestine refugees in Lebanon face a prohibition on working in 39 professions. A UN Special Rapporteur noted exclusion from syndicated professions such as law, medicine and engineering 'may be seen as prima facie discriminatory'.
energy_note: Qualified as a doctor, forbidden to practise.

description: Decree No. 17561 of 1964 governs employment of foreign workers and requires non-Lebanese including Palestinians to obtain work permits under conditions often impossible to meet. National preference rules plus the permit requirement make formal employment practically impossible, confining refugees to low-paid informal work with no labour or social protection.
energy_note: Permitted in principle, impossible in procedure.

aspect: The reforms that did not reach
description: In 2005 Lebanon lifted a ban on most clerical and technical posts subject to a temporary permit, but more than 20 high-level professions remained closed - medicine, law, engineering, pharmacy. 2010 amendments reduced some fees and eased reciprocity, with limited implementation.
energy_note: Two reforms, and the same professions still closed.

description: A 2010 study found just 37% of working-age Palestinians in Lebanon were employed. Those working illegally face wage discrimination - many employers pay less than Lebanese colleagues or refuse to hire at all.
money_note: Annual earnings gap versus a Lebanese peer.
energy_note: Thirty-seven per cent of adults, working.

aspect: It makes education a strange investment
description: Families still educate children who will not be permitted to practise. The degree becomes an emigration ticket or an ornament, and everyone involved knows it while doing it.
energy_note: A medical degree you'll never be allowed to use here.

aspect: For women it compounds an already low participation rate
description: Where formal work is closed and informal work is male-dominated manual labour, the remaining options for women narrow to domestic and piecework at the lowest rates in the economy.
energy_note: Excluded twice - as a refugee, then as a woman.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the 2005 reform that left the professions closed
description: In 2005 Lebanon lifted a ban on most clerical and technical positions subject to a temporary work permit, but more than 20 high-level professions remained off-limits - medicine, law, engineering and pharmacy among them. 2010 amendments reduced some fees and eased reciprocity requirements, with limited implementation.
energy_note: Two reforms, and the doctors still cannot practise.
